title: Encrypted DNS Provisioning RFC 9464 Wire Codec Architecture
purpose: Define the RFC 9464 ENCDNS_IP* and ENCDNS_DIGEST_INFO byte-level codec boundary without adding a full IKEv2 exchange implementation.
design_summary: The wire codec extends the scalar RFC 9464 helpers with deterministic IKEv2 configuration-attribute header encoding, ENCDNS_IP* field ordering, RFC 9460 SvcParam key/length/value encoding, reserved-bit-tolerant decoding, AliasMode rejection, CFG_REPLY/CFG_SET zero-address rejection, ENCDNS_DIGEST_INFO request/reply/set/ACK field ordering, registered-hash-identifier validation, and SHA2-256 SPKI digest computation over caller-supplied DER SPKI bytes.
data_and_state_considerations: The codec remains a pure DNS helper. It accepts and emits attribute byte arrays only; it does not perform IKEv2 negotiation, own resolver provisioning state, open encrypted DNS sessions, or validate certificates against a live TLS handshake.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The received IKEv2 reserved bit is masked before attribute type dispatch.
RFC 9460 SvcParams are normalized to strictly increasing numeric keys and duplicate keys are rejected.
ENCDNS_IP* service priority zero is rejected because RFC 9464 forbids AliasMode in this context.
ENCDNS_DIGEST_INFO CFG_ACK encodes and decodes only zero-length attribute data.
risks: This slice does not implement full IKEv2 Configuration payload framing or error-notify behavior.
This slice does not choose among provisioned resolvers, establish encrypted DNS sessions, or enforce split-tunnel policy.
This slice computes SHA2-256 over a DER SPKI input supplied by the caller; certificate extraction and validation remain out of scope.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: Keeping the byte-level codec in `Incursa.Quic.Dns` gives future IKEv2 integration a tested, trace-owned value codec while avoiding changes to QUIC transport packet, stream, scheduler, and TLS state machines.
